label: Red Hat RHCSA
cta_title: Free study guides for every Red Hat exam.

slides.title: Red Hat exams have *NO* multiple choice.

blocks.text: You get a live Red Hat Enterprise Linux system and a list of tasks. Nobody gives marks for knowing a command. You get marks only when the result **works and survives a reboot**.

rows: Partitions, LVM, file systems, swap, fstab
dnf repos, packages, containers with podman

blocks.text: Pass mark is *70%* (210 of 300). Every task is scored on the final state of the system.
Learn the order once: disk, then volume group, then logical volume, then file system, then mount.

lines: # 1. mark the partition, build the pool
# 2. carve out a volume (use -l 100%FREE for all space)

items: Make it permanent: add `/dev/vg0/lv0 /data xfs defaults 0 0` to */etc/fstab*, then run *mount -a* to test.
Grow later in one step: *lvextend -r -L +1G /dev/vg0/lv0*. The *-r* resizes the file system too.

blocks.text: XFS can grow but never shrink. For ext4 the resize tool is *resize2fs*.

slides.title: SELinux: *label it*, do not turn it off

blocks.text: If a service works as root but fails for users, the cause is usually a wrong SELinux label. Fix the label. Never leave SELinux disabled.

rows: Teaches the system the right label for a path
Applies the stored label to files

blocks.text: *chcon* changes a label only until the next relabel. Use *semanage fcontext* with *restorecon*.
Without *--permanent* the rule vanishes at reboot. Without *--reload* a permanent rule is not active yet.

items: *wheel* group members can use sudo on RHEL.
Set *ipv4.method manual* or the address is ignored.
Check the result with *ip a* and *nmcli con show*.

rows: Start now and at every boot
Check it will start after reboot
Pick the boot target: multi-user.target or graphical.target
Logs of one service since boot

blocks.text: **Forgot the root password?** A classic task. The steps:

lines: # at the GRUB menu press e, add rd.break to the linux line, Ctrl+X

items: **Read all tasks first.** Do the ones you know, then return to the rest.
**Reboot before you finish.** Anything not permanent is lost, and that is where most candidates fail.
**Use tab completion and man pages.** *man -k keyword* finds a command when you forget the name.
**Test each task** the way a user would: log in as that user, open that port, mount that disk.
**Do not turn off SELinux or the firewall** to make something work. It scores zero.

blocks.text: Practise on a VM you can break. Rebuild it and repeat each objective from memory.
